Most of the visible cost comes from React work around that update and a second wave after persistence.

| Finding | Evidence | Proposed solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding the card triggers a long render | `cardAdded` occurs about 50 ms after the click; the following React render lasts about **182 ms**. The click task lasts about **351 ms** overall. | Keep the update scoped to the affected column. Inspect the card and sortable components rendered within it for avoidable updates; measure again after each change. |
| Completion causes another broad render wave | About **1.3 s** after the click, a `changed` event is followed by React renders of roughly **152, 44, and 133 ms**. The trace shows `AppMenu`, action controls, and `NewCardDialog` work in this wave. | Remove redundant notifications and state updates. In particular, [closeDialog](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/shell/project/use_project_toolbar_menu_actions.ts) calls `setError(null)`, and [setError](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_session_service.ts) dispatches `changed` even when the error is already null. Make that operation a no-op when its state is unchanged. Then check whether form reset and dialog close can complete with fewer renders. |
| A watcher echo may do unnecessary project work | [reloadMarkdownFilesFromWatchEvents](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts) calls `importExternalCardFiles` after processing watched files; that function plans imports across the supplied file list. Expected writes already have a separate classification path. The trace shows later repository activity, but does **not** prove this scan caused the long render wave. | Instrument this path first. If it runs for the new card’s own write, skip the external-import scan once all watched changes are confirmed unchanged. Preserve handling for genuine external edits. |
| One insertion still scans collection data | [updateFiles](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_state.ts) filters the loaded files and card arrays; [dispatchCardChanges](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/data/data_service.ts) builds maps and compares all active cards. [useCardColumnCards](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/use_card_column_cards.ts) also filters cards and orders the target column. | If projects with many cards remain slow after the render fixes, update membership and order through the known changed card instead of scanning the full collection. This is a scaling improvement, not the clearest cause of this trace’s delay. |

The recording came from a Vite development page with extensive React and DevTools instrumentation, so these durations should **not** be treated as production timings. The strongest immediate targets are the repeated menu/dialog renders after completion and the expensive render following `cardAdded`. I made no code changes or ran tests.

Make that operation a no-op when its state is unchanged. Then check whether form reset and dialog close can complete with fewer renders.
   this needs definitely fixing

   why? is this really needed?
4. dispatchCardChanges builds maps and compares all active cards.
   why? is this really needed?
5. useCardColumnCards also filters cards and orders the target column.
   ordering makes sense, but why is it doing another filtering?

I’ll fix the redundant session notification first and check the dialog’s close sequence. Then I’ll inspect the card and sortable render path and trace the three collection scans to see which are needed for card creation and which serve other updates.

I fixed the redundant `changed` notification. [ProjectSessionService.setError](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/project_session_service.ts:375) now does nothing when the error is already clear and there is no pending conflict to clear. Its callers can still clear a real error or conflict. On successful creation, [NewCardDialog](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/shell/project/new_card_dialog.tsx:172) now resets the draft and closes the dialog in the same completion path, while preserving the immediate reset expected by existing tests.

I also removed one avoidable render per newly mounted card: [CardViewContent](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/card_view/project_card_view.tsx:86) now keeps its DOM element in a ref instead of React state. The card element still anchors menu actions. The sortable hook’s registration updates remain.

On the three scans:

- **`updateFiles`:** The filtering is needed by this general method to replace or remove existing files without duplicates, and to move changed cards into the correct active or background list. A known new card could use an insertion path, but that would need a separate change.
- **`dispatchCardChanges`:** The full comparison is how the shared callback detects additions, removals, and individual field changes for several kinds of update. For a known insertion, that work is redundant; I left it because changing the notification path affects more than creation.
- **`useCardColumnCards`:** The snapshot contains cards from all columns. The filter selects this column’s cards *before* `orderByAfter` orders them. Its add and remove subscription is already status scoped, so other columns do not rerender for this addition.

The targeted tests passed (**99 tests**) and `app` lint passed. I did not capture a new performance trace, so I cannot claim a measured millisecond improvement.

It sounds like a shortcut: instead of treating a new card the way it is supposed to, a generic 'fix all' approach is used? if so, this is not ok.

> dispatchCardChanges: The full comparison is how the shared callback detects additions, removals, and individual field changes for several kinds of update. For a known insertion, that work is redundant; I left it because changing the notification path affects more than creation.

> useCardColumnCards

You’re right: the create path already knows it has one new active card, so it should not run the generic replacement and collection diff logic. I’ll add a focused insertion path, keep the existing update path for edits and watcher changes, and test that creation emits only the expected card event.
